title: Zhiyi
hook: the founder of Tiantai, who ordered all the sutras into one great system

segments.voice: Yesterday, Patrul Rinpoche, the beggar teacher in the sheepskin coat. Did you manage one good thing nobody traced back to you? Today the story moves east, to China. Day nine hundred eighty-four.

A lot of kitchens have that one drawer. Batteries, twist ties, a key to nothing, a stack of takeout menus, a birthday candle. Everything in it is useful, and nothing can be found. Chinese Buddhists once had a drawer like that, only it was full of sutras. Teachings arrived from India and Central Asia over a long time, translated by different people, in no particular order. Some seemed simple, some soaring, and some seemed to say opposite things. Which one came first? Which one was the heart? A monk on a mountain set out to sort the whole drawer. Today, Zhiyi.
screen: `THAT ONE KITCHEN DRAWER.` → `A DRAWER FULL OF SUTRAS.` → `A MONK SETS OUT TO SORT IT.`

segments.voice: First, the man and the mountain. Zhiyi is honored as the founder of the Tiantai school, which takes its name from Mount Tiantai, where he lived and taught. Second, the sorting. Zhiyi's answer to the contradictions was not to throw any sutra out. Instead he arranged them as stages of the Buddha's teaching life, and as different kinds of teaching for different listeners. A doctor gives one patient a mild medicine and another a strong one, and both are right. In his scheme, the simpler sutras prepare the way, and the Lotus Sutra stands at the summit, where all the paths turn out to be one. Third, the practice behind the system. Zhiyi was not only a librarian of ideas. His lectures on meditation, written down by a student, are called Mohe Zhiguan, the great calming and contemplation. Calming settles the mind, like still water. Contemplation looks clearly at what's there. He taught them as two wings of one bird, and he wrote practical advice on posture, food, sleep and breath. Fourth, what a system is for. For Zhiyi, putting every teaching in its place was a kind of respect. Nothing was wasted, nothing was rejected, every sutra had a job. Other Chinese schools sorted the sutras differently, and Tiantai's order was not the only one. But his drawer, once sorted, could be opened by anyone.
screen: `A MONK ON MOUNT TIANTAI.` · `STAGES AND KINDS OF TEACHING.` · `CALMING AND CONTEMPLATION.` · `EVERY SUTRA HAS A JOB.` · then, large: `EVERYTHING IN ITS PLACE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: sort one messy thing, and today that thing is the mind. Settle, and let the breath calm down. That's the calming. Now, as each thought arrives, give it a quiet label and set it on a shelf. Planning. Remembering. Worrying. Hearing. Nothing gets thrown out. Each one just gets put where it belongs, and you come back to the breath. If the same thought keeps returning, label it again, gently. That's the contemplation: seeing clearly what's there. The bell holds the time.
Zhiyi. The founder of the Tiantai school, who ordered the sutras into one system with the Lotus Sutra at the summit, and taught calming and contemplation. Today's word.
Your line: everything in its place. Today, sort one messy drawer, shelf or inbox, and throw out less than you expected. Day nine hundred eighty-four.

howItsDone: In Tiantai (Tendai in Japan, Cheontae in Korea) communities, practitioners study the Lotus Sutra and Zhiyi's writings and practice calming and contemplation meditation as he described it.

fork.setup: two sutras seem to say opposite things. you're Zhiyi. what do you do?
options: decide one is fake and drop it
place each where it fits in the Buddha's teaching
fork.reveal: Zhiyi treated them like medicines for different patients: both right, each in its place, all leading to the Lotus Sutra.

original.note: Chinese zhiguan: calming and contemplation, the heart of Zhiyi's meditation teaching.

trapdoor: what you thought: a librarian who tidied up the sutras.
what it means: a founder who placed every teaching in a single path leading to the Lotus Sutra, and joined study to calming and contemplation.
what a scholar hears: Tiantai's classification of the teachings answered a real problem in Chinese Buddhism, sutras arriving out of order, and its zhiguan pairs the Sanskrit shamatha and vipashyana.

notes: The script avoids the numbers in 'five periods and eight teachings' under the claims rule; a Keeper may want them restored with a source.
The doctor-and-medicine image is an illustration; the Lotus Sutra uses skillful means images of its own. Confirm it fits Tiantai.
'Two wings of one bird' for calming and contemplation is commonly attributed to Zhiyi's writings on meditation; confirm.
Practical advice on posture, food, sleep and breath: from his shorter meditation manuals; confirm.
Original: 止觀 (traditional characters), pronounced roughly 'jih-GWAN' in Mandarin; confirm.
The howItsDone names Tendai and Cheontae; confirm.

Audit: Mohe Zhiguan was presented as a work Zhiyi wrote; it is his lectures recorded by his student Guanding, so the line now says so. The full 'five periods and eight teachings' scheme was systematized after Zhiyi; 'in his scheme' covers only the basic arrangement. Confirm.
